title: Attention Is All You Need
abstract: Introduces the Transformer, a sequence transduction architecture based entirely on self-attention, dispensing with recurrence and convolutions. The model achieves state-of-the-art machine translation quality while being far more parallelizable and faster to train, and its attention mechanism became the foundation of modern language models.

title: BERT: Pre-training of Deep Bidirectional Transformers for Language Understanding
abstract: Proposes BERT, which pre-trains deep bidirectional Transformer representations using masked language modeling and next sentence prediction. Fine-tuning the pre-trained model with one additional output layer achieves state-of-the-art results across a wide range of language understanding tasks including question answering and inference.

title: RoBERTa: A Robustly Optimized BERT Pretraining Approach
abstract: Shows that BERT was significantly undertrained and that careful choices of training data size, batch size, training duration, and removal of the next-sentence-prediction objective substantially improve downstream performance. The resulting recipe, RoBERTa, matches or exceeds all post-BERT methods of its time.

title: DistilBERT, a distilled version of BERT: smaller, faster, cheaper and lighter
abstract: Applies knowledge distillation during pre-training to compress BERT into a model 40% smaller and 60% faster that retains about 97% of its language understanding capability. Demonstrates that compact general-purpose language models are practical for on-device and low-latency applications.

title: Sentence-BERT: Sentence Embeddings using Siamese BERT-Networks
abstract: Modifies BERT with siamese and triplet network structures to produce semantically meaningful sentence embeddings comparable with cosine similarity. Reduces the cost of sentence similarity search from hours of cross-encoder inference to milliseconds of embedding comparison while maintaining accuracy, enabling large-scale semantic search and clustering.

title: MiniLM: Deep Self-Attention Distillation for Task-Agnostic Compression of Pre-Trained Transformers
abstract: Distills the self-attention distributions and value relations of a large Transformer teacher into a small student model, producing compact task-agnostic language models. MiniLM variants power many efficient sentence-embedding and reranking models used in production retrieval systems.

title: Text Embeddings by Weakly-Supervised Contrastive Pre-training
abstract: Presents E5, a family of text embedding models trained contrastively on a large curated corpus of weakly supervised text pairs. E5 provides strong general-purpose embeddings that transfer well to retrieval, clustering, and classification, outperforming prior embedding models on the BEIR and MTEB benchmarks.

title: Unsupervised Dense Information Retrieval with Contrastive Learning
abstract: Introduces Contriever, showing that contrastive learning without any supervision can train dense retrievers competitive with BM25 across many domains and languages. Establishes that unsupervised dense retrieval transfers robustly out of domain, addressing a key weakness of supervised dense retrievers.

title: Dense Passage Retrieval for Open-Domain Question Answering
abstract: Shows that dense passage representations learned from question-passage pairs with a dual-encoder outperform strong sparse baselines like BM25 for open-domain question answering. DPR retrieval improves end-to-end QA accuracy and established the dual-encoder plus FAISS pattern used by most subsequent RAG systems.

title: ColBERT: Efficient and Effective Passage Search via Contextualized Late Interaction over BERT
abstract: Proposes late interaction, encoding queries and documents into token-level embedding bags and computing relevance with a cheap MaxSim operator. ColBERT retains much of the effectiveness of full cross-attention BERT rankers while being orders of magnitude faster, bridging the gap between bi-encoders and cross-encoders.

title: ColBERTv2: Effective and Efficient Retrieval via Lightweight Late Interaction
abstract: Improves ColBERT with residual compression of token embeddings and denoised hard-negative supervision, cutting index size by an order of magnitude while improving quality. Demonstrates state-of-the-art retrieval effectiveness both in-domain and out-of-domain among efficient neural retrievers.

title: Retrieval-Augmented Generation for Knowledge-Intensive NLP Tasks
abstract: Introduces RAG, combining a parametric seq2seq generator with a non-parametric dense retriever over Wikipedia so the model conditions generation on retrieved passages. RAG sets state-of-the-art results on open-domain QA and produces more factual, specific generations, defining the retrieval-augmented generation paradigm.

title: REALM: Retrieval-Augmented Language Model Pre-Training
abstract: Augments language model pre-training with a latent knowledge retriever that is trained end-to-end through masked language modeling, backpropagating through retrieval over millions of documents. REALM substantially improves open-domain question answering and shows that retrieval can be learned jointly with the language model.

title: Leveraging Passage Retrieval with Generative Models for Open Domain Question Answering
abstract: Presents Fusion-in-Decoder (FiD), which encodes many retrieved passages independently and fuses them in the decoder of a seq2seq model. Performance improves steadily with the number of retrieved passages, achieving state-of-the-art open-domain QA and becoming a standard architecture for multi-passage synthesis.

title: Improving language models by retrieving from trillions of tokens
abstract: Introduces RETRO, which augments a language model with retrieval from a trillion-token database using chunked cross-attention over nearest-neighbor text. A 7B RETRO model matches much larger models on many benchmarks, showing retrieval can substitute for parameters at scale.

title: Atlas: Few-shot Learning with Retrieval Augmented Language Models
abstract: Studies retrieval-augmented models in few-shot settings, jointly training the retriever and language model. Atlas reaches strong performance on knowledge-intensive tasks with far fewer parameters than closed-book models, and analyzes what pre-training and index composition matter for few-shot RAG.

title: Self-RAG: Learning to Retrieve, Generate, and Critique through Self-Reflection
abstract: Trains a language model to decide when to retrieve, and to critique its own generations with special reflection tokens assessing relevance, support, and utility. Self-RAG improves factuality and citation accuracy over standard RAG by making retrieval adaptive and generation self-evaluating.

title: Corrective Retrieval Augmented Generation
abstract: Proposes CRAG, which evaluates the quality of retrieved documents with a lightweight retrieval evaluator and triggers corrective actions such as query rewriting and web search when confidence is low. Decompose-then-recompose refinement of evidence improves robustness of RAG against irrelevant or misleading retrieval.

title: Precise Zero-Shot Dense Retrieval without Relevance Labels
abstract: Introduces HyDE, which asks an instruction-following language model to write a hypothetical document answering the query and then retrieves real documents near its embedding. This zero-shot approach significantly outperforms unsupervised dense retrievers and is competitive with fine-tuned ones across tasks and languages.

title: Is ChatGPT Good at Search? Investigating Large Language Models as Re-Ranking Agents
abstract: Evaluates instruction-following LLMs as zero-shot listwise rerankers using a sliding-window permutation generation strategy. GPT-4-based reranking surpasses supervised cross-encoders on several benchmarks, and the paper distills this ability into smaller specialized rerankers.

title: RAGAS: Automated Evaluation of Retrieval Augmented Generation
abstract: Presents a reference-free evaluation framework for RAG pipelines measuring faithfulness of the answer to retrieved context, answer relevance, and context relevance using LLM-based judgments. Enables automated, fine-grained assessment of RAG quality without human-annotated ground truth.

title: Lost in the Middle: How Language Models Use Long Contexts
abstract: Shows that language model performance on retrieval-augmented tasks degrades substantially when relevant information sits in the middle of a long context, following a U-shaped position curve. The finding motivates reranking, context ordering, and context compression strategies in RAG systems.

title: Retrieval-Augmented Generation for Large Language Models: A Survey
abstract: Surveys the RAG landscape, organizing methods into naive, advanced, and modular paradigms and reviewing retrieval sources, query optimization, reranking, and generation integration. Summarizes evaluation frameworks and open challenges including robustness, attribution, and hybrid retrieval design.

title: Language Models are Few-Shot Learners
abstract: Introduces GPT-3, a 175-billion-parameter autoregressive language model, and shows that scaling enables strong task performance from natural-language prompts and a few in-context examples without gradient updates. Establishes in-context learning as a central capability of large language models.

title: Training language models to follow instructions with human feedback
abstract: Describes InstructGPT: supervised fine-tuning on demonstrations followed by reinforcement learning from human feedback (RLHF) to align language model outputs with user intent. Human evaluators prefer the aligned 1.3B model over the raw 175B GPT-3, showing alignment can matter more than scale.

title: LLaMA: Open and Efficient Foundation Language Models
abstract: Releases a family of foundation models from 7B to 65B parameters trained exclusively on publicly available data, with the 13B model outperforming GPT-3 on most benchmarks. Demonstrates that smaller models trained on more tokens are preferable at a given compute budget and catalyzes open LLM research.

title: Llama 2: Open Foundation and Fine-Tuned Chat Models
abstract: Presents Llama 2 and Llama 2-Chat, pretrained and RLHF-fine-tuned models from 7B to 70B parameters released for research and commercial use. Details the safety and helpfulness alignment methodology and shows chat performance competitive with leading closed models of its scale.

title: Exploring the Limits of Transfer Learning with a Unified Text-to-Text Transformer
abstract: Introduces T5, casting every NLP task as text-to-text, and systematically studies pre-training objectives, corpora, and scaling on the C4 dataset. The unified framework achieves state-of-the-art results across summarization, QA, and classification, and its encoder-decoder recipe underlies many retrieval and generation models.

title: Chain-of-Thought Prompting Elicits Reasoning in Large Language Models
abstract: Shows that prompting large language models with intermediate reasoning steps dramatically improves performance on arithmetic, commonsense, and symbolic reasoning tasks. Chain-of-thought ability emerges with model scale and became a core prompting technique for complex question answering.

title: Finetuned Language Models Are Zero-Shot Learners
abstract: Introduces instruction tuning: fine-tuning a language model on many tasks phrased as natural-language instructions. The resulting FLAN model substantially improves zero-shot generalization to unseen tasks, establishing instruction tuning as a standard alignment stage.

title: Scaling Instruction-Finetuned Language Models
abstract: Scales instruction fine-tuning to thousands of tasks and larger models, adding chain-of-thought data. Flan-T5 and Flan-PaLM show large gains in zero-shot, few-shot, and reasoning performance, with the public Flan-T5 checkpoints widely used for grounded generation in RAG systems.

title: Billion-scale similarity search with GPUs
abstract: Presents the algorithms behind FAISS for exact and approximate nearest-neighbor search on GPUs, including optimized k-selection and quantization-based indexes. Enables similarity search over billions of vectors and became the standard library for dense retrieval and vector databases.

title: Efficient and robust approximate nearest neighbor search using Hierarchical Navigable Small World graphs
abstract: Introduces HNSW, a multi-layer proximity-graph index enabling logarithmic-complexity approximate nearest neighbor search with excellent recall-speed trade-offs. HNSW underlies most modern vector search engines and approximate retrieval backends.

title: SciBERT: A Pretrained Language Model for Scientific Text
abstract: Pre-trains BERT on a large corpus of scientific publications with an in-domain vocabulary. SciBERT improves performance on scientific NLP tasks such as NER, relation extraction, and citation intent classification, demonstrating the value of domain-specific pre-training for research text.

title: SPECTER: Document-level Representation Learning using Citation-informed Transformers
abstract: Learns whole-document embeddings for scientific papers by training a Transformer with a citation-based triplet objective on titles and abstracts. SPECTER embeddings excel at paper recommendation, classification, and citation prediction without task-specific fine-tuning.

title: Learning Transferable Visual Models From Natural Language Supervision
abstract: Introduces CLIP, contrastively pre-training image and text encoders on 400 million web image-text pairs. The shared embedding space enables zero-shot image classification competitive with supervised baselines and general-purpose cross-modal retrieval.

title: LoRA: Low-Rank Adaptation of Large Language Models
abstract: Freezes pre-trained weights and injects trainable low-rank matrices into Transformer layers, reducing trainable parameters by orders of magnitude with no inference latency penalty. LoRA matches full fine-tuning quality and became the dominant parameter-efficient fine-tuning method.

title: QLoRA: Efficient Finetuning of Quantized LLMs
abstract: Combines 4-bit NF4 quantization of the base model with LoRA adapters and paged optimizers to fine-tune 65B-parameter models on a single GPU. QLoRA preserves full 16-bit fine-tuning performance, dramatically lowering the hardware barrier for adapting large models.

title: FlashAttention: Fast and Memory-Efficient Exact Attention with IO-Awareness
abstract: Reorders attention computation with tiling to minimize reads and writes to GPU high-bandwidth memory, computing exact attention faster and in linear memory. FlashAttention accelerates training and inference of Transformers and enables much longer context windows.

title: Toolformer: Language Models Can Teach Themselves to Use Tools
abstract: Trains a language model to decide which external APIs to call, when, and how, using self-supervised annotation of tool calls that reduce perplexity. Tool use improves zero-shot performance on tasks requiring calculation, search, and factual lookup without sacrificing core language ability.

title: ReAct: Synergizing Reasoning and Acting in Language Models
abstract: Interleaves chain-of-thought reasoning traces with actions against external environments such as search APIs, letting reasoning guide acting and observations ground reasoning. ReAct improves question answering and decision-making tasks and defines the standard loop for LLM agents.

title: RAPTOR: Recursive Abstractive Processing for Tree-Organized Retrieval
abstract: Builds a retrieval tree by recursively clustering and summarizing text chunks, allowing retrieval at multiple levels of abstraction from details to holistic summaries. RAPTOR improves QA over long documents, particularly for questions requiring multi-step or whole-document understanding.

title: From Local to Global: A Graph RAG Approach to Query-Focused Summarization
abstract: Introduces GraphRAG, which extracts an entity knowledge graph from a corpus, detects communities, and pre-summarizes them so global sensemaking questions can be answered by map-reduce over community summaries. Substantially improves comprehensiveness and diversity of answers to corpus-level questions compared with vector-only RAG.

title: Longformer: The Long-Document Transformer
abstract: Replaces full self-attention with a combination of sliding-window local attention and task-motivated global attention, scaling linearly with sequence length. Longformer processes documents of thousands of tokens and improves long-document classification, QA, and summarization.

title: Transformer-XL: Attentive Language Models Beyond a Fixed-Length Context
abstract: Adds segment-level recurrence with state reuse and relative positional encodings to Transformers, enabling dependencies far beyond a fixed context window. Transformer-XL learns 80% longer dependencies than vanilla Transformers and substantially improves language modeling perplexity.

title: Sparse, Dense, and Attentional Representations for Text Retrieval
abstract: Analyzes the trade-offs between sparse lexical, dense dual-encoder, and multi-vector attentional retrieval, showing theoretically and empirically how dense encoders lose fidelity on long documents. Proposes hybrid and multi-vector models that combine the strengths of sparse and dense representations for text retrieval.
